propositions: The CLI verb `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` must validate all SHAs against the repository before recording a COMMITS event; if any SHA is invalid, the entire batch is rejected with an all-or-nothing guarantee and no event is recorded.

The deterministic close-gate check in close_precheck.py must block ticket closure if any discovered commit (from COMMITS events or rebar-trailer referencing) modifies a path not covered by the union of file_impact declarations across the ticket and its transitive descendants, unless the path matches an exemption glob (tests/**, docs/**, **/*.md, CHANGELOG.md).

Merge commits must be explicitly skipped during close-gate validation because git show --name-only produces an empty or combined diff for merges, and merges author no changes themselves; reading them as path-less would silently pass.

Source-(i) SHAs from COMMITS events that are absent locally must be skipped (not blocked), while source-(ii) local commits reachable via rebar-trailer must fail closed if git show fails, preventing false negatives and false positives respectively.

The shared glob-matching helper with **/‑aware semantics must be hoisted to src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py and imported by no rebar.llm modules; existing copies in prompts.py and registry.py must become thin delegating wrappers.

The attach_commits surface must be exposed consistently across CLI (verb + handler in _ARGV_REGISTRY), library (rebar.attach_commits re-exported), and MCP (registered tool with AttachCommitsResultOut outputSchema), all validating via the shared seam in _lib_writes.py.
